questions.question: Explain transmittance and absorbance—define both, derive their relationship, and interpret their significance in practical colorimetric analysis.
questions.solution_html:
• Explain transmittance and absorbance—define both, derive their relationship, and interpret their
  • significance in practical colourimetric analysis /
  • • Definitions: Transmittance (T): Fraction of incident light that passes through a sample. 𝑇 =
  • 𝐼/𝐼0. . Absorbance (A): Logarithmic measure of light absorbed. 𝐴 = log⁡10(𝐼0/𝐼).
  • • Relationship Derivation : 𝐴 = log⁡10(𝐼0/𝐼) = log⁡10(1/𝑇) = −log⁡10 𝑇.
  • • Significance: Absorbance is directly proportional to concentration (Beer-Lambert Law: 𝐴 =
  • 𝜖𝑏𝑐). . This enables the use of a calibration curve to determine unknown concentrations,
  • thereby forming the basis of quantitative analysis. -
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025
questions.final_answer: thereby forming the basis of quantitative analysis.
